newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says Kenya summit part of Anglo-Saxon plot.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says Kenya summit part of Anglo-Saxon plot.

text.p: Francophone Zaire said on Tuesday that the Nairobi summit was a masquerade put together by an alliance of English-speaking countries which were seeking to destabilise it.
"There were an impressive number of countries at the summit who have nothing to do with the Great Lakes, giving it a falsely international character," Information Minister Boguo Makele told Reuters.

"After analysing documents in our posession it seems that the initiative for this meeting is not African and that in effect a foreign power directly implicated in the events in the east is the author of this masquerade," he added.
"We denounce this Anglo-Saxon coalition which is going about destabilising Zaire and the African continent."
Boguo did not specify which non-African country was behind the summit but members of the government have accused the United States of backing Rwanda with logistical help.
Zaire did not attend the summit hosted in Nairobi by Kenyan President Daniel Arap Moi on Monday to resolve a Central African crisis which has sprawned a revolt in eastern Zaire.
The government says the summit was a bid to divert attention from Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda's role in the revolt by forcing Zaire into talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Since the revolt began in October, the government has refused to recognise Kabila as a rebel leader, dismissing him as a pawn in the hands of an expansionist coalition of Tutsi forces from neighbouring countries.
